_comment: The launch flags the agent passes the research browser (ADR-0001 variant C2, M2-5).
Every entry here has been verified behaviourally on Edge Beta 153 by the scripts in
tests/security/windows-enforcement/ -- see edge-integration/README.md for what each one
was measured doing. Nothing enters this file on the strength of documentation alone: a
switch or policy name the browser does not recognise is accepted silently and changes
nothing, which is indistinguishable from working until someone measures it.
Candidates awaiting verification live in the README, deliberately not here.
A second Edge installation at its own image path, which is the whole of variant C2.
Windows per-app network controls key on the image path only, so this path -- not a
profile, not a command line -- is what the agent's WFP rules bind to. It MUST match the
path those rules use or enforcement silently covers nothing.

placeholders.ResearchProfileDir: Absolute path to the dedicated research profile directory. Separate from the analyst's ordinary Edge profile. Note this separates state, NOT network identity -- see README.
placeholders.AgentProxyPort: The port the agent's loopback proxy actually bound. Ephemeral by default (Mina:Agent:LoopbackPort = 0), so it is discovered at runtime and passed here; nothing may hard-code it.

_comment: Empty by design, and that is a decision rather than an omission. Edge reads policy from
one machine-wide location that every channel and every profile shares, so any policy set
for the research context also lands on the analyst's ordinary Edge. The controls below
are pinned and available, but the research browser is already confined to the agent's
proxy by WFP, so setting them machine-wide degrades ordinary browsing to duplicate a
control that is already in force. See README 'Why no machine-wide policies'.
